newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK provisional December M0.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK provisional December M0.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing M0 money supply rose a provisional 0.9 percent m-m in December and 7.1 percent y-y, vs expected 0.7 pct and 7.1 pct respectively.

"The numbers are probably a little bit softer than expected, but notes and coins were up a strong 7.4 percent which is consistent with the view the Christmas period was relatively strong in terms of retail sales."

"The bottom line is...the underlying picture is still one of strong money growth and potentially strong retail sales to come. These numbers won't change the views of those looking for a rate hike next week."

"Month by month changes don't correlate very well with retail sales but the fact that M0 remains buoyant suggests there is no sign of retrenchment on the consumer side. It's all pointing in the same direction -- consumers remain buoyant and are prepared to take on more debt. With lower taxes coming, the housing market flourishing and any interest rate rises unlikely to be severe, there looks like there is little on the horizon to change that picture."

"The notes and coins rose a weaker than expected 0.7 percent, but nonetheless it was still consistent with a fairly buoyant month on the high street. I think it's the first statistical proof of previous anecdotal evidence of a decent month for retailers in the run up to Christmas.
"At the margins it will probably add to pressure for a rate rise but we'll really have to wait for the CBI distributive trades survey...and the true retail sales figures."
